contest.title: Luxury Bathroom Design Competition
contest.description:
1. THE CHALLENGE

We seek an exceptional interior designer, interior architect, or architectural designer to completely reimagine our existing master bathroom. This is a real renovation, not an exercise in producing attractive pictures. Our ambition is an extraordinary space with the sophistication, originality, and attention to detail of a world-class luxury hotel or architecturally significant private residence.

We want to be surprised. Show us a solution we would not have imagined ourselves: remarkable spatial planning, beautiful proportions, distinctive materials, layered lighting, and ingenious storage. A memorable design need not be extravagant or expensive for its own sake. Exceptional taste and architectural judgment matter more than decoration.

The winner may be considered for a separate paid design-development project. Designers worldwide are welcome; a professional architecture license is not required for this conceptual competition.

2. CREATIVE FREEDOM

We have no preferred floor plan or prescribed design style. You may rethink fixture locations, partitions, circulation, cabinetry, and the use of the adjacent utility space. We welcome restrained, bold, warm, minimal, sculptural, or unexpected approaches. Do not assume we want a particular bathroom trend or arrangement.

Our priority is to see genuinely independent ideas. We will supply existing-condition information, not our earlier conceptual renderings. The finished space must be both spectacular and comfortable for everyday use.

3. EXISTING SPACE AND MEASUREMENTS

The bathroom has an irregular footprint comprising a main rectangular area and a left-side extension. Previously recorded PRELIMINARY dimensions are:

- Main bathroom: 150 x 200 inches (381 x 508 cm).
- Existing shower: 50 x 60 inches (127 x 152 cm).
- Adjacent mechanical area: 50 x 40 inches (127 x 102 cm).
- Combined left-side extension: 50 x 100 inches (127 x 254 cm).
- Toilet enclosure: approximately 36 x 60 inches (91 x 152 cm).

The main rectangle plus a separate, nonoverlapping 50 x 100-inch extension would total about 243 sq ft. That figure is only an estimate, NOT a verified measured area. Exact geometry, door/window positions, wall thicknesses, ceiling height, and relationships between spaces must be checked against the supplied original sketch and walkthrough video. Where information is missing or inconsistent, clearly state your assumptions or ask a question.

Do not enlarge the room in renderings, invent windows, or silently change structural boundaries. Your proposed plan must be dimensionally credible and your renderings must depict that same plan.

4. EXISTING PLUMBING AND UTILITIES

The current bathroom has a bathtub, separate shower, double vanity, and enclosed toilet. A nearby mechanical area houses a water heater and other equipment.

We prefer to keep plumbing near its existing locations when practical, but this is a preference, not an absolute restriction. Relocation is acceptable when it creates a meaningful improvement in design or function. You may consider reclaiming some or all of the mechanical space if equipment can be moved or a tankless water heater proves feasible. Do not assume the utility space is available without explaining the dependency.

Clearly identify major plumbing, electrical, mechanical, or structural changes in your proposal. We appreciate smart construction choices, but do not want modest cost savings to prevent an exceptional result.

5. REQUIRED FUNCTIONS — STORAGE IS A MAJOR PRIORITY

Every proposal must include:

- BATHTUB: A comfortable full-size tub suitable for regular bathing.
- SHOWER: A generous, beautiful, practical shower.
- DOUBLE VANITY: Two sinks, usable counter space, and functional cabinetry.
- PRIVATE TOILET: An appropriately private toilet area; retaining its current location is preferred.
- SUBSTANTIAL STORAGE: This is extremely important. We need generous, organized, readily accessible storage for towels, toiletries, personal-care items, grooming appliances, cleaning supplies, and everyday necessities. Consider full-height cabinetry, deep drawers, concealed compartments, recessed storage, custom millwork, and other inventive solutions. Show where items actually go. Storage must not be sacrificed to make a rendering look minimalist, nor should it make the space feel crowded. The ideal room looks serene because clutter has a proper home.
- LIGHTING: Layered architectural and ambient lighting plus effective task lighting at the vanities and other key areas.
- COMFORTABLE CIRCULATION: Sensible clearances, door swings, access to storage, and easy daily use.

The arrangement of these functions is entirely your decision. We are not prescribing a relationship between the bathtub and shower or any specific enclosure type.

6. WHAT WILL IMPRESS US

We are looking for a unified architectural idea, not a collection of fashionable fixtures. Strong entries will demonstrate:

- Original spatial thinking and a distinctive visual identity.
- Elegant proportions and a convincing sense of luxury.
- Excellent materials and harmonious transitions between finishes.
- Thoughtful natural, indirect, accent, and task lighting.
- Beautiful custom cabinetry with genuinely useful storage capacity.
- Functional details that support daily use and maintenance.
- A timeless result that does not depend on fleeting trends.

We welcome bold gestures when they improve the overall composition. Avoid excessive ornament, gratuitous complexity, and features that are impressive only in a single camera angle.

7. CONSTRUCTION REALISM

This is intended to be a high-end renovation, and we are willing to invest in quality materials, fixtures, and custom work. However, the construction budget is not unlimited. Identify major cost drivers, unusual installation requirements, and any assumptions about moving plumbing, modifying walls, or accessing utility space. We do not need a contractor's estimate at this stage.

Designs should consider realistic fixture dimensions, access, ventilation, waterproofing, and safe circulation. Final technical and code compliance will be reviewed with local professionals; this contest is for design concepts, not stamped construction documents.

8. REQUIRED COMPETITION DELIVERABLES

A complete entry must include ALL FOUR items below:

A. DIMENSIONED FLOOR PLAN
A legible proposed plan showing the actual footprint and key dimensions; doors and windows; tub, shower, toilet, and both sinks; approximate fixture sizes; partitions; major storage cabinets and built-ins; and principal circulation clearances. Identify any proposed use of the mechanical area. Include enough dimensions to demonstrate that the design fits.

B. AT LEAST TWO HIGH-QUALITY 3D VIEWS
Show the overall architectural concept and at least one additional perspective highlighting important features. Communicate the materials, lighting, and storage integration. BOTH images must depict the SAME design shown on the floor plan. Attractive images that contradict the plan will not qualify.

C. SHORT DESIGN EXPLANATION
Explain the core idea, what makes it distinctive, how it improves daily use, how substantial storage is provided, and what significant plumbing, mechanical, or structural changes are proposed.

D. MATERIAL PALETTE
Present the primary materials, finishes, colors, and textures. Exact product links and detailed specifications are not required for the contest.

We value clarity and substance over elaborate presentation packaging. One excellent, fully coordinated concept is better than several superficial variations.

9. AI-ASSISTED WORK

AI tools are welcome for exploration and visualization. But generic AI-generated bathroom images without accurate spatial planning are not acceptable. Verify the design using CAD, measured 3D modeling, or another credible dimensional method. Disclose substantial generative-AI use and briefly explain how you checked the geometry. We will judge design quality, not software choice.

10. WHAT NOT TO SUBMIT

Please avoid stock or copied imagery; generic luxury bathrooms unrelated to our space; layouts with missing required fixtures; inadequate storage; invented floor area; implausible clearances; renderings that disagree with the plan; and multiple near-identical AI variations. A polished rendering cannot compensate for a poor or unbuildable design.

11. JUDGING CRITERIA

30% — ARCHITECTURAL CREATIVITY AND VISUAL IMPACT: Originality, sophistication, memorability, and overall beauty.

30% — SPACE PLANNING, FUNCTIONALITY, AND STORAGE: Smart use of the footprint, practical fixture arrangements, realistic clearances, and ample well-integrated storage.

25% — MATERIALS, LIGHTING, AND AESTHETIC QUALITY: Cohesion, material selection, architectural detail, and atmosphere.

15% — CONSTRUCTION PRACTICALITY: Respect for the existing building, clear identification of major changes, and reasonable buildability.

The winner will not necessarily have the most photorealistic images. The strongest overall design will win.

12. POTENTIAL PAID FOLLOW-UP

After the competition, we may hire a participant for a separate paid engagement to refine the selected design. Potential scope includes accurate plans and elevations, cabinetry/storage detailing, lighting layout, fixture and finish selections, additional visualizations, and documents for contractor pricing. Full construction documentation is NOT required to enter this contest. Winning does not guarantee further work.

13. DESIGNER EXPERIENCE

We welcome designers worldwide and value exceptional portfolios over credentials. Experience in luxury interiors, hospitality, spas, and space planning is especially relevant.

14. FINAL INVITATION

We want ideas we have not considered. Create a bathroom that feels extraordinary yet works beautifully every day. Make storage as intelligent as the architecture. Surprise us.  And lastly in the video there is a window.  That window can be left there or deleted, your choice.
